dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?
Hi, Tony. Yes, um, this is Rosa Morales. I'm calling about my water and sewer bill. It came in the mail yesterday and, well, it's higher than I expected, and I'm not happy about it.
Okay, I can take a look with you. What's the service address?
359 Annandale Road, up in the North End. I rent the downstairs, so the bill comes in my name but the landlord and I, we go back and forth about it.
Got it, give me one second to pull that up. [pause] Okay, Ms. Morales, I've got the account. Looks like the latest bill covers a full quarter, and the usage is up some from the one before.
Up some. I'm one person, Tony. I don't run a laundromat. I wash a load of clothes maybe twice a week, and I've been awake since five this morning and I can tell it, so forgive me if I sound short.

No, no, you're fine. Let me explain how it reads. The bill is based on the meter reading, and the sewer charge follows the water you use. So when the water number goes up, the sewer part goes up right along with it.
So it's the same number twice, more or less.

More or less, yeah. Two charges that are tied to the same meter reading. If you want, I can have someone check whether the reading was an actual one or an estimate, and whether there's any sign of a leak, like a running toilet.
A running toilet. Well, now that you say it, the one in the back does run a little after you flush. I told the landlord in the fall.
That could do it. A toilet that runs can add up a lot over three months and you'd never see it. It's worth getting fixed, and that's something you'd want to bring up with your landlord again.
Oh, I will. Believe me. Now, while I have you, is there any kind of discount? For low income, or for older people? I'm in my sixties and I'm on a fixed income, and every bill is a squeeze.

There are some assistance programs and senior options that the city or the state can offer, but I don't have the details of who qualifies in front of me. I can send you the information, or transfer you to somebody in the office who handles that. Which would you rather?
Send it, please. Mail is fine. I like to have it on paper so I can read it slow.
Sure. I'll note the account to mail the information to 359 Annandale. Anything else?
Yes. My daughter helps me with the bills. She does the computer part, she's better at that than me. She wants to be able to call and ask questions on my behalf. How do I get her authorized?

Good idea. Usually we need something in writing from you, naming her and giving her okay to talk about the account. I can note on the account that she's going to be calling, but she'd likely need that written permission on file to get details.
Written, all right. Does it need a special form, or just a letter?
A signed letter with your name, the address, and her name and phone number should be a good start. If the office wants a form, they'll tell her. She can drop it off at City Hall or mail it.
Okay, I'll have her write it up tonight. She gets off work late, so everything with us happens at night.
That's how it goes for a lot of folks.

Which brings me to another thing. If I want to pay this bill and I'm not able to get down there during the day, is there a phone line I can call at night to pay? Like an automated one, that works after you close?

Yes, there's a way to pay online through the city's website anytime, and I believe there's an automated phone option as well. There's also a drop box outside City Hall for checks. I can give you the number for the phone payment line if you have a pen.
Hold on, let me find one. [pause] Okay, go ahead, slowly now.

Tell you what, the number is printed on the bottom of your bill, near the payment stub. It's easier to read it from there than for me to say it and have you miss a digit. Your account number is there too, and you'll need that to pay.
Oh, the stub. I see it now. It's tiny, but I see it.
Yep, that's the one. And if the phone line doesn't take you right through, your daughter can help you on the website.
She will. All right. So you'll mail the discount information, and I'll get the letter for my daughter, and I'll tell the landlord about the toilet again.
That's it. And if you want the reading checked, call back and we'll set that up.
I might do that after the toilet is fixed, see if the next one comes down. Thank you, Tony. You explained it plain, I appreciate that.
Happy to help, Ms. Morales. Try to get some rest today.
I'll try. Goodbye now.
